correctness.rationale: The beta=1 recurrence is copied from Eq. (2) of the exact 2023 source. P(x)=s-kx/[H(H+x)] is strictly decreasing and yields a unique interior equilibrium. Exact Jacobian sign and characteristic-polynomial identities show an attracting prey-only equilibrium and a positive saddle. The strict wedge bounds give x_n <= x_0 exp(n-B(q^n-1)) and y_n>=y_0 q^n. This implies all exponential-weighted x-series converge. Telescoping the y equation defines positive L, and summable tails yield sum|y_n-Le^{sn}|<infinity. With sum(x_n y_n)<infinity the corrected logarithm of x converges to positive K. Uniform convergence yields continuity; lower bounds show L nonconstant. Full proof is in RESULT.md; verify.py passed exact rational and high-precision finite diagnostics, not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Full text of Hong–Zhang 2023 supplies the map, local fixed-point stability and Neimark–Sacker analysis but not an invariant high-predator wedge, simultaneously a prey-only sink, and its two finite discrete scattering amplitudes. Parshad et al. 2022 rigorously establish predator explosion for a related no-refuge ODE, not these discrete-time limit expressions or finite-sink coexistence. Ghosh et al. 2017 study the corresponding differential equation, not the iterative asymptotic clocks. Targeted published-finding corpus claim searches found related but not logically dominating records. Originality remains best-knowledge subject to the stated search/coverage risks.

value.rationale: The 2023 discrete refuge model was investigated mainly by local equilibrium and Neimark–Sacker methods. This theorem establishes a genuinely global high-predator trapping regime in which runaway and a nearby finite prey-only sink coexist for the same fixed parameters. Two positive initial-state-dependent scattering amplitudes and the exact order-n correction in a double-exponential prey clock capture detailed behavior impossible to extract from the known qualitative continuous-time predator-explosion theorem or from local equilibrium stability. It is a motivated dynamical limit rather than an arbitrary finite computation; no global basin census is claimed.
